Welcome to Winchcombe School
At Winchcombe School, we are proud to offer a caring, ambitious and inclusive learning environment where every student is supported to thrive. We set high expectations, while recognising and responding to the individual needs of our students, helping each one grow in confidence, character and ability.
Our broad, balanced and enriching curriculum is designed to challenge and inspire. Underpinning everything we do are our core values: Attitude, Stewardship, Pride, Integrity, Resilience, Enjoyment and Success. We expect our students not only to understand these values, but to live them every day.
As a community school, we are deeply committed to nurturing aspiration and personal development. One of our great strengths lies in the strong relationships between staff and students. We know our students well and work hard to provide the personalised pastoral care, safeguarding and guidance they need to flourish.
Our school is set in a beautiful location, with modern facilities and a welcoming atmosphere. As a smaller-than-average secondary school, students quickly feel part of our close-knit community. We support every student through their journey from Year 7 to Year 11, ensuring they are well prepared for the next step, whether that’s Sixth Form, college, an apprenticeship or other pathways. Many go on to some of the region’s top post-16 providers, where they continue to build on the strong foundations laid here.
At Winchcombe School, we empower every student to leave us confident, capable, and ready to make a meaningful contribution to the world.
Every day is an Open Day! We are happy to arrange tours of the school with a prior appointment (made via email admin@winchcombeschool.co.uk or phone 01242 602233). There is no better way to see a school than when it is in action!
We are delighted that Ofsted has recognised Winchcombe School as meeting the Expected Standard in all areas, confirming that the school is providing a good quality of education, care and support for its pupils. The inspection highlighted the significant improvements made across the school and the strong foundations now in place to support continued success.
Inspectors found that pupils are proud of their school, feel safe, and benefit from positive relationships with staff. The report notes:
“Pupils at Winchcombe School are very proud of their school. They know that adults will help and support them with their learning and their wellbeing.”
The inspection recognised the school’s ambitious curriculum, improved behaviour, and inclusive culture. Ofsted praised the way staff support all learners, particularly those with additional needs, ensuring that pupils make positive progress and are increasingly well prepared for their next steps in education, employment and training.
A particular strength identified by inspectors was the school’s commitment to personal development and careers education:
“The careers programme is a strength of the school.”
Inspectors highlighted the wide range of opportunities available to students, including work experience, leadership roles, extracurricular activities, educational visits and enrichment programmes that help pupils develop confidence, character and ambition.
The report also acknowledges the substantial improvements made to behaviour and attendance. Ofsted noted that pupils understand the school’s high expectations and that:
“Lessons are calm and pupils can learn without disruption.”
Inspectors recognised the determination shown by leaders in driving school improvement, praising the swift action taken to strengthen the curriculum, improve attendance and enhance the quality of education. They also highlighted the positive culture amongst staff, noting that:
“Staff have great faith in the leadership of the school and are proud to work there.”
The report further reflects the confidence families have in the school:
“Parents are highly positive about the school. They praise the recent improvements in behaviour, the caring approach of staff and the wide range of extracurricular opportunities available for pupils.”
We are proud that the inspection recognises the hard work of our students, staff, governors, Trust and wider community. While celebrating these achievements, we remain committed to continuous improvement and ensuring every pupil can thrive, achieve success and be fully prepared for their future.
WHAT CAN WE OFFER?
Broad Curriculum– we want students to experience a diverse range of subjects enabling them to discover their interests and talents
Pastoral Support – growing up is not easy! We have a dedicated pastoral support team who work closely with both students and their families
Varied Opportunities– we seek to enhance our curriculum with visits and extra-curricular opportunities to enable our students to ASPIRE for SUCCESS
As a popular and growing school, we have seen recent investment in our facilities: we now boast a refurbished Dining Hall and Auditorium. Our sporting facilities are exceptional with a Sports Centre; access to a full size 3G Astroturf pitch, alongside a wealth of open fields.
The School is dedicated to ensure every pupil has the same opportunities. In the past 18 months, we have provided over 80 laptops to pupils for use at home.
To apply for a place please visit our Admissions area
OUR VALUES
OUR MISSION
We empower every student to discover their potential, embrace opportunities, and achieve success. Through high expectations and strong support, we equip our learners with the knowledge, skills and confidence to thrive in an ever-changing world.
OUR VALUES
We are driven by a clear purpose: to nurture ambitious, compassionate and resilient young people who contribute positively to society. Our core values — Attitude, Stewardship, Pride, Integrity, Resilience, Enjoyment and Success — underpin everything we do. We encourage our students to live these values each day, shaping their character and future.
OUR ETHOS
We are a vibrant, inclusive community where every student is known, valued and inspired to excel. We believe that success is built on respect, kindness, and a strong sense of belonging. By fostering curiosity, creativity and a love of learning, we create an environment where students are confident to explore their passions, overcome challenges and celebrate achievements.
OUR COMMITMENT
We are committed to developing well-rounded individuals equipped with the academic foundation and personal skills to flourish. Our rich, broad curriculum ensures every student builds strong literacy and numeracy skills while discovering new interests and talents. We work in partnership with families and the wider community to support each student’s wellbeing, academic progress and personal development, preparing them for lifelong success.

Careers Advisor
Careers Advisor Appointments
We use the services of an external professional to work with our students on a 1-1 basis for their personalized careers advice.
Appointment information
Data To enable the Careers Advisor to tailor the advice to each student, they have access (in school only) to student’s Bromcom data showing grades and attendance.
Evaluation Each student’s experience is evaluated using an internal reflective cycle questionnaire. This captures their thoughts before, during and after the meeting. Initially, comments made before the meeting are used to help the Careers Advisor with a starting point for discussion. Follow-up comments are used by the Careers Lead to see where additional support would be useful for a student, and to track the effectiveness of the service. A summary of this data (anonymized) is shared with the Careers Advisor.
Safeguarding If a safeguarding issue arises in the meeting with the Careers Advisor, they will inform the school’s safeguarding Team immediately, in line with school policy, and also inform the Careers Lead. The Careers Lead make a record of the concern.
Example Careers Advisor feedback form
Personal Guidance evaluation form
Staff
I am a level 7 qualified Careers Lead, and this role is part of my middle leadership responsibilities, alongside running a curriculum area and teaching full time. My background is in Finance, with specialism in financial planning, marketing and staff training. Throughout my career I have always worked in some capacity so have experience of most forms of work including voluntary, part & full time, fixed term contract, zero hours, consultancy, mentoring, counselling and coaching. Currently my voluntary work is as a steward for The Rose theatre, Tewkesbury. I am an active member of the Gloucestershire Careers & Employability network group and currently part of a working party to improve and develop the provision of careers fairs for students. At national level, I have been involved with projects around LMI, evaluating statutory provision and Gatsby benchmarks, and linking careers to the curriculum. In January 2024 I completed my enhanced Careers Leadership training with the CEC (Careers and Enterprise Company) which enabled me to up date my knowledge and work with other Careers Lead to share and develop resources.
In my role as Careers Lead, I work with external agencies to ensure the successful transition of our students, foster links with employers and post 16 providers, monitor our provision against the Gatsby benchmarks and ensure we meet the statutory requirements.
It is always wonderful to see our young people confidently progress to the next step of their career and it is especially rewarding to be able to welcome so many of our alumni back to share their success stories with current students.
Employability Assistant: Mrs Sarah Edwards
In addition to working as Personnel Officer in school, I help support Careers, using my experience of organising interviews for our school staff recruitment to give Year 10 students practice in mock interviews, as well as helping Miss Willmott with other Careers events.
I’ve lived in Winchcombe for over twenty years and our sons came to this school (one is now a primary teacher in London and the other is studying to be a dentist).
During my own career I have worked in both the public and private sectors in various roles, including working overseas for several years. I have a BA (Hons) degree in French and am qualified to teach English as a Foreign language. I have done voluntary work and fundraising for both schools in the town and have built up a good network of friends and professionals locally who are kind enough to help with our school initiatives. I believe that it is important for young people to cultivate a broad range of interpersonal skills while they are at school – as well as their academic subjects – and am delighted to help improve their confidence with our Careers initiatives here. I enjoy finding out what our alumni have gone on to do after leaving and put together a ‘Where are they now?’ board in school – hopefully as an inspiration to our current students!
Careers Advisor: Mrs Alison Williams
I am a Level 7 qualified, registered Careers Advisor (QCG). I have two teenage children and have been working in Careers for around 8 years now having previously gained over fifteen years of experience as an HR professional, including HR Consultancy, Adult Employability and Outplacement. I’ve worked abroad and have experience in many sectors, giving me a broad understanding of what employers are looking for.
I love my role which I see as a means of enabling young people to open their eyes to themselves and opening their minds to the world of opportunities open to them. Thinking about all these opportunities can be overwhelming so I try to help them to clarify their options and start out on a suitable path through the “forest” which most find very useful.
Work Experience (WEX) Co-Ordinator: Amy Keen
In addition to my role as Pastoral Support Lead for key stage 4, I took over the Work Experience Co-ordinator role in October 2024. Part of the exciting changes that I am making is to introduce Unifrog as the digital platform for WEX. This encourages students to take responsibility for finding, checking, recording and evaluating their WEX. I will monitor their progress and be on hand to advise with finding placements. I have lived in the local area for over 15 years, which gives me a good understanding of the local opportunities for WEX and an understanding of the challenges of transport.
I studied at the University of Gloucestershire, graduating in 2007 with a BA Hons in Sociology & Psychology. My career has been in the Health & Social Care sector, supporting both adults and children with a variety of issues from finding work and housing, to finances and improving social skills and independent living skills. This included working with adults with learning disabilities and difficulties. Most recently I worked in a school for children with special needs, so have an appreciation of the challenges this brings and the support needed to help a young person transition into the work place.

English Language & Literature
English Language & Literature
Aim/Vision
The curriculum for English is designed so students develop their understanding of both Language and Literature skills, building their skillset and deepening their knowledge year on year as they move from KS3 to KS4. In KS3, each year group studies a novel, poetry, fiction and non-fiction extracts, a play, and undertakes both creative and transactional writing, mirroring the units at GCSE. Texts from the 19th, 20th, and 21st century are all studied. Our curriculum is based around the core principles of what, how, and why: this a is a model that underpins the way we teach students to structure their responses, but also shapes the approach in each year – Y7 introduces and reinforces authorial methods – what; Y8 deepens analytical skill – how; Y9 explores authorial intention in greater detail – why. By KS4, these skills are embedded and reflexive. We shape our lessons around learning questions rather than objectives, designed to encourage independent thought and curiosity that sparks personal, critical responses from students. Throughout our curriculum, units are linked by ‘golden threads’ – the big thematic concepts that are shared between works of literature and non-fiction alike, such as power, duality, social injustice, and fate vs. choice. Our intention is for students to grow a love of literature and the written or spoken word; to understand how the things we read and write reflect the state of the world around us, and how they capture the essence of the human experience – alongside the technical capability to comprehend, analyse, and construct their own powerful words. They will develop the ability to understand different perspectives and critical thinking skills, allowing insightful personal responses. They will develop cultural capital through exploration of important socio-cultural concepts in different times and cultures, and learn how to question ideas effectively.
Learning Journey
Assessment
Formative (in-class)
All classes at every stage are continually assessed through recall quizzes, teacher questioning, peer- and self-assessment, whole class feedback, and comment marking.
Reading and Writing assessments based on the studied units are set once a year in the Spring term. These include a test on content from the Knowledge Organiser.
All KS3 students sit the GL reading test in the Summer term which tests reading comprehension skills.
Mock exams for both Language and Literature are held at four points through the course.
Y10 – Spring term Shakespearean play, Language Paper One
Y10 – Summer term Unseen Poetry, Blood Brothers, Language Paper Two
Y11 – Autumn term Language Paper One, Poetry Anthology
Y11 – Spring term 19th Century Novel
We follow the AQA syllabus for English Literature and English Language.

Good for low-stakes, chunked recall and revision

Video lectures to extend learning

Breakdowns of plots, characters, themes, and more!
Collins Snap Revision Guides – offered for purchase through the school in Y10 or Y11 at a reduced rate.

Computer Science
Computer Science
Aim/Vision
In years 7-9, students study Computing for 1 or 2 hours a fortnight. If students opt to study Computer Science in Years 10 & 11, they follow the AQA GCSE Computer Science curriculum.
Learning Journey
Assessment
Students sit end of unit assessments in all years. In Years 7, 8 and 9, students sit 2 summative assessments per year.
At GCSE, students sit end of unit assessments.
In year 10, students sit two exam-style assessments in Autumn and Summer.
In year 11, students sit one or two mock papers before their final exams in the Summer of Y11.
